subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation HDI stand for?
options: Human Development Index
Household Development Indicator
Human Distribution Index
Human Diversity Indicator
questions.explain: The HDI (Human Development Index) is a composite measure used to compare the level of development between countries.

questions.q: The Human Development Index (HDI) combines which three measures into a single value?
options: Life expectancy, education and income (GNI per capita)
Birth rate, death rate and migration
GDP, unemployment and inflation
Literacy, population density and urbanisation
questions.explain: The HDI brings together health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling) and wealth (GNI per capita) to give a fuller picture than income alone.

questions.q: What does the development indicator GNI stand for?
options: Gross National Income
Gross National Investment
General National Index
Global National Income
questions.explain: GNI (Gross National Income) is the total value of goods and services earned by a country, often expressed per capita to compare development.

questions.q: Why do many landlocked countries tend to experience slower economic development?
options: They have no direct access to the sea, increasing the cost of importing and exporting goods
They always lack any natural resources
They receive no aid from other countries
They automatically have larger populations than coastal countries
questions.explain: Without a coastline, trade must pass through neighbouring countries, raising transport costs and limiting economic growth.

questions.q: Which historical process, in which powerful nations controlled and exploited other territories, is a major cause of uneven development?
options: Colonialism
Urbanisation
Industrialisation
Globalisation
questions.explain: Colonialism drained resources and wealth from many colonised regions, contributing to a long-term development gap.

questions.q: A country with a very high infant mortality rate is most likely to also have which of the following?
options: Limited access to healthcare, clean water and sanitation
A highly developed, high-income economy
Excellent, widely available medical services
The lowest birth rate in the world
questions.explain: High infant mortality is closely linked to poor healthcare, unsafe water and sanitation, so it is a useful indicator of low development.

questions.q: Country X has a GNI per capita of around US$900, a high birth rate and a low life expectancy. Using standard income classification, Country X is best described as a:
options: Low-income country (LIC)
High-income country (HIC)
Country with no development gap
Newly emerging economy near the top of the development scale
questions.explain: A very low GNI per capita combined with a high birth rate and low life expectancy indicates a low-income country.

questions.q: Bilateral aid is best described as aid that is:
options: Given directly from one government to another government
Given through international organisations such as the World Bank
Raised entirely by charities from public donations
Only ever given as emergency food supplies
questions.explain: Bilateral aid passes directly from one country's government to another, often with conditions attached.

questions.q: Multilateral aid is aid that is:
options: Given by governments to international organisations, such as the UN or World Bank, which then distribute it
Given directly from one country to another with no third party
Provided only by small local charities
Always in the form of loans repaid with high interest
questions.explain: Multilateral aid is pooled by many donor governments through international organisations before being distributed.

questions.q: A key disadvantage of tied aid for the receiving country is that:
options: The donor sets conditions that mainly benefit the donor, such as buying the donor's goods
It can never be used to build any infrastructure
It is always given as immediate emergency relief
It must be fully repaid within a single year
questions.explain: Tied aid comes with conditions, such as spending it on the donor's own products, which reduces its benefit to the receiver.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of short-term (emergency) aid?
options: Food, water and shelter provided immediately after an earthquake
Funding to build a new school over several years
A long-term programme to train local nurses
A loan to construct a hydroelectric dam
questions.explain: Short-term emergency aid provides immediate relief such as food, water and shelter following a disaster.

questions.q: Why is intermediate (appropriate) technology often more successful in lower-income countries than large-scale schemes?
options: It uses low-cost, sustainable methods that local people can build and maintain themselves
It relies entirely on foreign engineers to operate it
It requires expensive imported machinery to work
It is designed to produce the greatest possible profit for TNCs
questions.explain: Intermediate technology is affordable and suited to local skills, so communities can sustain projects themselves.

questions.q: A charity works with a small village to install hand pumps that residents are trained to repair themselves, with decisions made by the local community. This is an example of:
options: A bottom-up (small-scale) development project
A top-down (large-scale) government scheme
Emergency relief aid
Tied bilateral aid
questions.explain: Bottom-up projects are small-scale and led by local communities, giving them control over decisions and maintenance.

questions.q: An organisation such as Oxfam or WaterAid is best described as a:
options: Non-governmental organisation (NGO) that is independent of government control
Branch of the United Nations
Government department responsible for overseas aid
Transnational corporation that trades for profit
questions.explain: NGOs are non-profit, non-governmental bodies that often deliver aid and development projects funded by donations.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation TNC stand for?
options: Transnational Corporation
Trade and National Commerce
Transitional National Company
Total National Capital
questions.explain: A TNC (Transnational Corporation) operates in more than one country, linking economies through trade and investment.

questions.q: How does Fairtrade certification directly help producers in lower-income countries?
options: It guarantees them a minimum price for their goods regardless of market fluctuations
It removes all import taxes on their exports
It gives them free machinery from TNCs
It guarantees them jobs in higher-income countries
questions.explain: Fairtrade guarantees producers a stable minimum price, protecting them from falling global market prices.

questions.q: Globalisation is best described as:
options: The growing interconnection of the world's economies, cultures and populations through trade and communication
The movement of people from rural areas to towns and cities
The process of a country becoming a low-income country
A reduction in the amount of trade between countries
questions.explain: Globalisation is the increasing links between countries through trade, investment, communication and the movement of people.

questions.q: A TNC opens a new factory in a low-income country. Which of the following is a likely positive impact for the host country?
options: The creation of jobs and an increase in local incomes
An immediate rise in the country's HDI to match that of an HIC
The complete elimination of all environmental problems
A guarantee that all of the company's profits stay in the host country
questions.explain: TNCs bring employment and wages to host countries, although much of the profit often returns to the company's home country.

questions.q: Global interdependence means that:
options: Countries rely on one another for trade, resources, investment and support
Countries are completely self-sufficient and do not trade
Only high-income countries depend on other countries
Aid is the only link that exists between countries
questions.explain: Interdependence describes how countries depend on each other economically, socially and politically through trade and cooperation.

questions.q: A low-income country spends a large share of its income repaying interest on international loans, leaving little for schools and hospitals. This situation is best described as:
options: The burden of debt acting as a barrier to development
A clear example of successful long-term development aid
A direct benefit of Fairtrade
The result of using intermediate technology
questions.explain: Repaying large debts diverts money away from services such as health and education, slowing a country's development.
